title: A currency factory that hands out cached instances

blocks.text: A factory method **does not have to create a new object**: `Integer.valueOf()` returns cached instances, and the page recommends caching when the products are immutable. Callers then get the same object for the same value.
Write the immutable `Currency` with a private constructor and:

items: `Currency.of(String code)` returns **one cached instance per code**. A code must be exactly three capital letters `A`-`Z`; anything else throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

cases.says: Currency.of("EUR") returns the same instance on every call, and different codes give different instances.
A code built at run time gets the same instance as the literal code, because the cache is keyed by value.
A code that is not exactly three capital letters A-Z, such as EURO, eu, E1R, EUR followed by a newline, ÄÖÜ or null, throws IllegalArgumentException.

concepts: A factory method may return cached instances, as Integer.valueOf does, when the products are immutable.
